chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no believer who lends to a believer, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, except that Allah will record for him his reward by accounting it as charity until his wealth returns to him.'

key_terms.أَجْر: Reward; spiritual recompense for good deeds
key_terms.إِقْرَاض: Lending money or goods with the expectation of repayment
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Charity; voluntary giving for the sake of God
key_terms.وَجْهَ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah; seeking divine pleasure and countenance

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for lending money to a fellow Muslim in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to emphasize that lending for Allah's sake is an act of worship equal in reward to charity until the debt is settled. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that financial transactions, when performed with pure intention (ikhlas), transcend mere civil contracts and become enduring spiritual investments. The hadith thus encourages believers to view lending not just as economic assistance but as a sustained act of piety.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is none from a Believer who lends to a Believer, seeking by it the Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Reckon for him his Recompense by accounting it as a charity (on his behalf) until his wealth returns to him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from Rib’iy ibn ‘Abd Allah from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘For every believing person who provides a loan for another believing person, for the sake of Allah, Allah counts its reward as that of giving charity until the time the loan is paid back.’”
